cohort: 100 pregnant women undergoing elective cesarean delivery at Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
finding: Compared to hyperbaric bupivacaine, isobaric bupivacaine for spinal anesthesia in elective cesarean section resulted in greater hemodynamic changes, including a higher incidence of hypotension and increased vasopressor requirements.
mod_finding: Isobaric bupivacaine during cesarean section led to greater blood pressure changes, hypotension, and vasopressor use than hyperbaric bupivacaine.
